text:
I am like that unknown island,
beating as lush trees rock it,
in the middle of a sea
that does not understand me,
surrounded by nothing,
alone, only alone.

On my island are shining birds,
painted by angel painters;
there are beasts that look at me tenderly,
and poisonous flowers.

There are poet streams
and inner voices
of sleeping volcanoes.

Perhaps there is some treasure
deep in my depths.
Who knows whether I have
a diamond in my mountain,
or only a small
piece of coal!

The trees in my island's forest
are you, my verses.
How lovely you sound sometimes
when the great musician, wind,
plays you as the surrounding sea comes in!

If someone reaches this island that I am,
I hope they find something here:
springs of glowing verses
and cascades of peace are what I have.

A name rises through my soul
and will not let me weep my secrets;
and I am happy land, for I have the art
of being happy and poor at once.

It is a pleasure to be unknown,
an unknown island in the eternal ocean.
At the center of the world, without a book,
I know everything, for a messenger came
and left me a cross for life
—and for death, a mystery.
